mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces earnings visibility and increases risk premia, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases both discount rates and input costs, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a strengthening residential demand channel, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports broader equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during three consecutive months where HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates a statistical artifact or data inconsistency rather than economic improvement; this anomaly is associated with elevated market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises while UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of RSAFS declines.
